requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The one marked test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. It checks every content obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions.content`.

The test runs a first `search_text` call with an empty result (pattern "absent"). It parses the `instructions` string and asserts that the string contains each of these phrases:
- "Before submitting, close every delivered search page". This maps to the obligation to call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting.
- "finish_search". This names the tool.
- "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read". This maps to how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence.
- "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result". This maps to passing `used: []` when none contributed.
- "without reading more source". This maps to finishing a page recording the selected inputs without fetching more source.

The test also asserts that the first `search_structure` call from a fresh session returns the identical instructions, and that later searches and continuation pages omit them. The requirement says "the instructions supplied under `first_search.instructions`", so this shows the same content is supplied in both search kinds. Delivery rules such as the first successful search only and omission on later pages belong to the parent requirement.

The assertions are substring checks on the real delivered string. They would fail if any of the five required ideas were dropped. The wording is not pinned exactly, which matches the requirement: it states content obligations, not exact text. I found no untested obligation and no wrong expectation, so I report no gap.
